A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. The shared content can be matched reliably, including renumbered displays. Appendix sections A–C are present in v2 but absent from the supplied v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-estimation experiments on 3DPW, 3DHP and EgoBody, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original runtime measurements, VLM-label evaluations, EMA sensitivity results and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The motion-text alignment, frozen encoders, global-rotation handling, EMA updates, missing-keypoint completion and overall objective remain the same. Appendix B documents the existing labeling and verification stage; it does not establish an algorithmic addition.

E1.justification: Human3.6M training and 3DPW, 3DHP and EgoBody evaluation remain unchanged. Section 5.5 adds an explicit semantic-input failure scenario, evaluating pose adaptation with incorrect VLM labels versus correct oracle labels. No new dataset or domain is introduced.

E2.justification: The matched benchmark comparisons retain their baselines. The motion-discriminator and unpaired-local-pose alternatives in v1 Table 3 reappear in v2 Table 4 with clarified names and unchanged results. Added runtime and qualitative comparisons use existing comparators.

E3.justification: Existing backbones, pose metrics and training settings are retained. New analyses introduce a 5,000-frame labeling audit, incorrect-label/oracle/no-adaptation controls, per-frame runtime evaluation and an EMA grid from 0.75 to 0.95. The newly specified OpenPose threshold documents an existing setting rather than establishing changed preprocessing.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis beyond the retained component and fill-in ablations. It adds VLM failure and oracle-label tests, EMA sensitivity, runtime analysis, CLIP-based label verification and qualitative case studies across all three evaluation datasets (Section 5.5 and Appendices A–C).

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The new labeling accuracy and audit sample size are point-result and evaluation-design information, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark, component-ablation and fill-in-threshold scores are unchanged. Substantial new results include 107.6 versus 74.1 ms runtime for the proposed method and CycleAdapt (Table 5), 96.4% labeling accuracy, and failure-case MPJPE of 213.8 initially, 92.2 with incorrect labels and 83.7 with oracle labels (Table 7). EMA, label-verification and qualitative results are also added.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 corrects the smoothing-target definitions beneath Eq. 9: v1 assigns motion denoising to beta-bar and averaged shape to theta-bar; v2 assigns them to theta-bar and beta-bar, consistent with Section 3.1. This is a local definition correction; the loss sum remains equivalent and no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and principal conclusion retain the same claims: semantic motion guidance and text-aligned 2D completion improve test-time pose estimation, including more than 12% PA-MPJPE reductions on 3DPW and 3DHP. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains resilience to erroneous labels through the alignment regularizer being constrained by 2D projection supervision. It adds an interpretation of EMA sensitivity and identifies motion blur and residual directional ambiguity as unresolved issues. Earlier limitations concerning motion timing and MotionCLIP generalization remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies substantial previously unavailable labeling details: GPT-4o identity, prompts, dictionary constraints, downsampling, CLIP consistency checking at 0.3 and manual correction. Section 5.2 also specifies the OpenPose confidence threshold of 0.3. Conversely, Section 4.1 drops v1's explicit stride-1 specification without stating a replacement.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MHEntropy, ExtPose, pose-estimation calibration and blurry-image hand reconstruction. Section 5.4 narrows its statement about absent semantic approaches to TTA. The MotionDiffuse publication update is the same cited work, and the main research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained. Changes include localized language and cross-reference corrections, a rewritten explanation of semantic comparison strategies, a clearer qualitative caption, a failure-case subsection, appendices and publication/acknowledgment text.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime, label-failure and EMA tables; a fill-in quantity/PCK chart; labeling examples and a similarity heatmap; and extensive qualitative/failure panels. Existing ablation tables are reordered, while v1 Figure 4 becomes v2 Figure 5 with larger presentation, clearer highlights and an expanded caption.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves its central semantic-labeling process largely undocumented in the supplied PDF and does not examine labeling failures or runtime. v2 makes prompts, verification and human correction inspectable, while adding targeted reliability, efficiency and sensitivity evidence. This substantially improves reproducibility and assessment of the method's central dependency without weakening the retained benchmark evidence. Manual correction still limits conclusions about fully automatic deployment, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but these residual limitations do not outweigh the gains.
